audit_findings.title: Post-anchor debt-funded cash may be counted without its economic cost
audit_findings.magnitude: $10.000 million debt issued, $9.804 million cash added, and $0.614 million initial annualized interest; bridge exposure up to $0.95 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds June 2026 cash, while FY2025 equity-level OE contains neither the new loan's interest cost nor a deduction for its principal.
audit_findings.evidence: On March 13, 2026, Artesian Water Maryland and CoBank entered into a Master Loan Agreement, or the MLA, and supplement to the MLA, in which CoBank will make a single loan to Artesian Water Maryland in a principal amount not to exceed $10 million.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated date-matching error, not merely a possibility. The six-month filing reports $10.000 million of new debt and a $9.752 million cash increase, leaving $9.804 million of cash at June 30. Counting that cash while omitting the associated post-anchor financing obligation can overstate scenario equity values by about 3.3%-4.4%.
audit_findings.action: Trace the loan proceeds and rerun with a matched-date bridge: either exclude debt-funded cash or deduct the unmatched debt principal, or replace FY2025 OE with an equity-OE measure that includes the loan's financing cost and deployment economics.

audit_findings.title: The maintenance-capex allowance may be structurally too low
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; filed 2026 net utility-plant investment is $64.281 million, 3.55 times the $18.1 million OE anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Any recurring replacement, compliance, or mandatory-relocation expenditure omitted from maintenance capex directly overstates OE and every forecast and terminal-value year derived from it.
audit_findings.evidence: We expect that our net investments in utility plant in 2026 will be approximately $64.3 million.
audit_findings.explanation: No maintenance-capex error is demonstrated because the record does not separate maintenance from expansion or establish corresponding developer funding and rate recovery. Nevertheless, the $64.281 million program, aging infrastructure, PFAS work, and $21.060 million of scheduled 2026-2028 mandatory relocations make a structurally material shortfall reasonably possible.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the OE maintenance deduction project by project against the 2026 program, classifying replacement, compliance, relocation, capacity growth, developer contributions, settlement funding, and regulator-approved recovery; rerun all scenarios using the recurring owner-funded amount.

audit_findings.title: AFUDC could leave non-cash construction returns in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: up to $2.379 million of annual OE, including $1.640 million equity AFUDC and $0.739 million debt AFUDC; 13.1% of the anchor and mechanically $2.73-$3.61 per share of operating value
audit_findings.mechanism: Retained AFUDC inflates anchor OE with a non-cash construction return and then propagates through forecast growth and terminal value while construction spending is also handled through capex.
audit_findings.evidence: Allowance for Funds Used during Construction, or AFUDC, is a non-cash credit to income with a corresponding charge to utility plant that represents the cost of borrowed funds or a return on equity funds devoted to plant under construction.
audit_findings.explanation: The filed AFUDC amount is material, but the supplied record does not include the OE worksheet, so retention is not demonstrated. If all $2.379 million remained in the anchor, the mechanically affected operating PV would be approximately $28.3-$37.3 million across the scenarios.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct FY2025 OE from the ledger and cash-flow statement, showing separate treatment of equity and debt AFUDC, interest paid, and capex; remove AFUDC exactly once and rerun the valuation if any remains.

audit_findings.title: Finite customer obligations may be capitalized as perpetual equity earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $26.301 million regulatory liabilities and $1.299 million FY2025 regulatory-liability amortization; the amortization equals 7.2% of anchor OE and mechanically $1.49-$1.97 per share of operating value
audit_findings.mechanism: If regulatory-liability amortization or associated tax benefits remain in normalized OE, a finite customer credit is grown and capitalized in terminal value as though it were perpetual equity earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: Regulatory liabilities represent excess recovery of cost or other items that have been deferred because it is probable such amounts will be returned to customers through future regulated rates.
audit_findings.explanation: The customer obligation and annual amortization are filed, but the missing OE reconciliation prevents a demonstrated-error finding. If the $1.299 million FY2025 benefit was retained and perpetuated, approximately $15.4-$20.4 million of scenario operating PV would be affected; the $26.301 million liability itself should not automatically be deducted without modeling its rate and cash effects.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile FY2025 OE to the $1.299 million amortization and related tax-rate adjustment, then model scheduled customer rate reductions or demonstrate a complete offset in cash flows before rerunning.

audit_findings.title: The FY2025 anchor contains provisional rate economics
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified beyond the filed $2.248 million reserve for customer refund at June 30, 2026, including a $1.854 million increase during the first six months of 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: Any temporary-rate revenue ultimately disallowed but not reserved in FY2025 would reduce normalized OE; refund interest or customer credits would create additional cash costs.
audit_findings.evidence: If any such rates are found to be in excess of rates the DEPSC finds to be appropriate, the utility must refund customers the portion found to be in excess with interest.
audit_findings.explanation: The June 2026 filing confirms that the rate case remained unresolved and that the refund reserve grew materially, but recorded reserves already reduce reported revenue. The record does not identify the final allowed rates or quantify any FY2025 exposure beyond amounts already reserved, so an additional valuation error and its materiality cannot yet be established.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the final DEPSC order effective by the valuation date, reconcile final allowed revenue and refund interest to the $2.248 million reserve and FY2025 temporary-rate revenue, and rerun only for any unreserved FY2025 amount.

audit_findings.title: An unrecorded litigation claim sits ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $3.400 million claim, equal to $0.33 per share and 1.2%-1.5% of scenario equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: An adverse uninsured and unrecoverable judgment would be a one-time cash claim ahead of common equity and therefore reduce the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: While we plan to defend the claim vigorously, it is possible that we could incur a loss; however, any loss is not estimable at this time.
audit_findings.explanation: No loss is demonstrated or estimable, and the June 2026 filing reports no resolution or accrual. Even treating the entire $3.400 million claim as an immediate equity deduction would reduce value by only about $0.33 per share, leaving the $21.78-$28.42 valuation range below the $36.19 market price.
audit_findings.action: Check subsequent proceedings, defense costs, insurance coverage, and rate-recovery eligibility; revise the bridge only if a probable or determinable net exposure emerges.
